exposure: Karyotype with a second or third cell line with more than one X
Cardiac status at preconception (risk factors for poor pregnancy outcomes)
outcome: Pregnancy-related aortic dimension changes (growth at sinuses, ascending aorta)
Long-term impact of pregnancy on TS-related comorbidities
cohort: The study included 156 TS patients, with a median age of 32 years, including individuals with mosaic karyotypes such as 45,X/46,XX, 45,X/47,XXX, and 45,X/46,XX/47,XXX.
finding: 13.5% of Turner Syndrome patients experienced spontaneous pregnancies, predicted by specific mosaic karyotypes and spontaneous menarche, and while aortic diameters increased significantly during pregnancy, no aortic dissections were observed in this cohort during or in the years after pregnancy.
